answer: Where the work can be checked by a machine, I'd take the vote out of it completely. If the task is a code fix, the network runs a hidden test suite. If it's a volume estimate for a karst sinkhole, it reruns the math on the raw survey points. Pass and you get paid, fail and you don't, no matter how many accounts call it great. Someone can spin up a thousand mirror accounts, but none of them can vote a broken answer into passing, so every clone still has to do the real work. Peer votes only stay for fuzzy stuff, like whether a travel blurb about an evening zephyr reads well.
